conditions.why: an N-step COUPLED weight trajectory, with the two sides actually moving. ITS OPERATING POINT, added pass 390 (R154) because '20 steps, coupled, 89.21 %' reads as if the update rule were swept and it was not: in this arm the LR is a strictly linear ramp reaching 11.4 % of peak, never the knee at 1000 or the decay at 50000; the clip coefficient is exactly 1.0 at all 20 steps and all 80 per-sample coefficients, 12.5703x below the threshold; participation_spread is [4] at every step, so the per-parameter divisor is a uniform scaling Adam cancels; n_disabled_last_sample is 0 at every step; and weight_decay is 0.0, which is upstream's own default. That is five factors single-valued or inert, and it is PROTOCOL's factorisation working rather than a hole -- the four state-free factors are driven with a controlled input EXACTLY because a real batch never hits their corners. Two of the five are covered outside this artifact and are named as such: the non-uniform participation divisor only by superseded arms, and the disabled-parameter path only by COVERAGE's 5oid datapoint. Full map, computed from the artifacts: perf/of3t_orchestrator/trajpoint/TRAJ_OPERATING_POINT.json.

checks.why: at least the 20 steps of3t-traj20 pre-registered

the span of the widest single boundary capture the campaign holds -- upstream's own float64 gradient mass inside diffusion_module. The most a trajectory can cover without a capture spanning more than one section. 100 % of that module is 9.170528876862544 / 10.279642678524981 = 89.2105802084 % of the model, so the bar is the measured ceiling ROUNDED DOWN (D209: pass 355 wrote 89.2106, which rounded the ceiling UP and made the clause unreachable by construction -- full coverage of the module missed it by 0.0000198 points). MET at pass 357: of3t-trajfull reads 89.21058020840096 over 761 of 761 reference tensors, having named the 180 the scoring previously could not (96 diffusion_transformer.blocks.N fused qkv split on the scoring side, 42 atom_attn_enc and 42 atom_attn_dec lazily uploaded per-block weights, 0 absent). At this boundary the clause is now equivalent to `score every reference tensor`

the scope must be ONE capture composed forward, not a union of per-section runs. A union tests each update rule in isolation and none of the coupling, and the two are indistinguishable in a pct_of_model_sq_grad_norm field. Emitted from pass 357 by of3t-trajfull as six computed checks, not a literal -- the decisive one being that at k=2 Adam's first update is -lr*sign(g) elementwise, so the two sides' displacement signs agree on 93.96 % of 201,279,424 elements where a side advanced from the other's gradient would agree on 100 %

checks.actual: 19 of 20 step(s) move upstream-side, ours moves at every one
checks.why: the campaign's own lesson, repaired at pass 319 (D169): an arm that never moves proves nothing about the update rule, so OUR side must move at every step where THEIRS does. This read `d1.zero_both_sides is False` until pass 319 and that clause was UNSATISFIABLE by any faithful reproduction -- upstream's AlphaFoldLRScheduler warms up linearly from base_lr=0.0, so lr(0) == 0.0 exactly and step 1 leaves the weights bit-identical on BOTH sides with a non-zero gradient (D169_FIRST_STEP_IS_A_NO_OP.json). The replacement is strictly stronger: it reads all 20 steps rather than the one that carries no information, and it is not satisfied by the live artifacts being any closer than they were
